meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'razor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня с собой даже бритвы нет.
examples.trans: I don't even have a razor with me.
All right, runt, take my razor.

бывать.gloss: to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit

meanings.en: to happen, to exist, there can be
meanings.note: 3rd person бывает = there is / can be
Часто бывать где-то. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit', paired with 'быть'.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

examples.trans: Seems not, we are not rushing.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

достать.gloss: to take out, to get, to reach

meanings.en: to take out, to pull out, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

meanings.en: to get hold of, to obtain
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

examples.trans: And take his eye out with a spoon.

examples.text: Вы понимаете, что вы нас достали уже?

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some, any', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He is asking for some delicious dessert.
The guest wants some light salad.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hers' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?

пользоваться.gloss: to use, to take advantage of

meanings.en: to use, to make use of
meanings.note: + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'льзоваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to use, to take advantage of', paired with 'воспользоваться'.
+ instrumental: пользоваться слабостью

examples.trans: You're taking advantage of my weakness!
Of course I am. It's blackmail.

meanings.note: To do with the family. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емейный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('family').

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Perfective of мочь. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be able, to manage', paired with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Тогда она не сможет тебя упрекнуть.
examples.trans: Then she won't be able to reproach you.
